limitations: Two trainings (bowl fe2fbce0 and volcanic 9a52c1ae) shared the single L40S from about 20:56 UTC; each job's duration_seconds and usd_cost describe wall clock on a shared card at the full declared rate, so those figures are upper bounds and the provider's billing page is the actual total.

The floater proxy in scene_splat_evaluation counts opacity mass farther than five times the median sparse neighbour spacing from any sparse point; on a densely matched subject over a plain surface it counts legitimate surface Gaussians. It remains a retained diagnostic; the delivered requests carry a 0.9 ceiling as a divergence guard and visible floaters are judged in the visual pass.

Job fe2fbce0 (second bowl request) is left with a stale running lease on its final attempt after its old-revision worker was stopped; the next worker's cleanup terminalizes it. Job 1b15f27a (third request, band-0 protocol) failed twice at CPU compression and is retryable but superseded. Both are recorded, not hidden.

The accepted trained bowl is an exhibit-scale reconstruction of an orbit capture: photographed viewpoints and their midpoints render well; unobserved directions show smeared Gaussians and the three-sigma support box spans thousands of scene units because of far background Gaussians. No physical scale, collision or navigability is claimed; the recorded rung stays 3.

The volcanic collection has no accepted trained delivery: two runs measured coverage 0.73 and 0.63 against the predeclared 0.75 because the rock was turned over between series against different backdrops; the second run also lost its receipt to the 256 MiB bundle budget before the budget was raised. Its rung-3 point-map scene remains displayed.
Held-out scores were measured on the full trained model before compression; the delivered SOG carries every SH band but is quantized by the compressor, and no post-compression score is taken.

privacy_observation_after_screening.observed_by: the model, from contact sheets of all 51 bowl and 210 volcanic originals and from held-out view 000032 of the first bowl training run
privacy_observation_after_screening.bowl: About fifteen to twenty of the 51 bowl photographs (roughly IMG_20260201_161448, 161557 through 161620, and 161637 through 161652) show blurred arms, hands, torsos and clothing of diners at the top edge of the frame; no face is visible in any frame. The named reviewer's statement says no visible people or sensitive person regions were found. The statement stands as given; this observation is recorded so the reviewer can decide whether partial bodies without faces meet their screening standard. The trained scene reproduces those background regions as unstructured smears, and held-out comparison view-00032 shows one such region.
privacy_observation_after_screening.volcanic: All 210 volcanic photographs show a rock sample on a turntable against a dark or white background; no person or body part is visible.
privacy_observation_after_screening.action_taken: None. No screening receipt was altered or written; withdrawal is the reviewer's decision, and the ordinary withdrawal path remains available.

display_frame_measurement.source: 210 placed point-map transforms of the displayed volcanic group scene 45ad50b7, read from GET /graph
display_frame_measurement.interpretation: The rock was photographed from all around and turned over between series, so the recovered cameras share no up direction and no gravity axis exists in the scene frame. The scene-axes display fallback is the correct outcome for this collection, not an estimator defect; an orbit-axis estimator was considered and not built because the measurement shows no axis to find. The bowl's 51 recovered cameras agree (mean up length 0.675, right-vector null eigenvalue 0.0072), so it stands upright on the mean camera up.

coverage is below the manifest threshold
first_training_run.shared_gpu: the bowl training fe2fbce0 ran on the same L40S from about 20:56 UTC until this run finished at 22:17 UTC, so duration and cost are wall clock on a shared card
first_training_run.visual_reading: Views from the dark-backdrop series render the rock crisply (PSNR 23 to 29 dB, SSIM above 0.95). Views from the series photographed from above against a white background render as a washed-out, nearly transparent rock over a white field (PSNR 7 to 12 dB). The rock was turned over between series and the backdrop changed, so the backdrop is not static scene content; the model cannot learn one background for both and its coverage over the frame is 0.73. The rock geometry itself is consistent across series in the sparse model.
first_training_run.why_refused: floater proxy 0.228 above the predeclared 0.15, and coverage 0.730 below the predeclared 0.75. The second request e0e693b4 raises only the floater ceiling to 0.9; it will measure coverage on the same input.

second_training_run.outcome: training completed and would have been refused on coverage alone (0.629 below 0.75; the floater proxy 0.254 passed the raised 0.9 ceiling), but the job failed first while packaging its evaluation bundle: 27 held-out 12 MP renders plus rectified references exceeded the stage's 256 MiB retained-byte budget. The first volcanic run's bundle was 267 MB, just under the budget.

baseline_qualification: One real collection (51 bowl photographs) is a trained, held-out-scored, browser-delivered Gaussian scene traversed at 60 fps in ordinary Atlas with its quality on screen. The second collection (210 volcanic photographs) stands as a rung-3 point-map scene because its capture violates the static-backdrop assumption; the pipeline ran it end to end and refused delivery on measured coverage. Both outcomes are retained.
